articles.title: Why Connecting AI With Physical Robots Is More Difficult Than It Looks
articles.excerpt: Artificial intelligence has advanced faster in image recognition, natural language processing and decision support. Robotics has continued to evolve through improved motors, controllers, sensors and m…
articles.body: Artificial intelligence has advanced faster in image recognition, natural language processing and decision support. Robotics has continued to evolve through improved motors, controllers, sensors and mechanical configurations. Combining these technologies sounds simple. Provide a robot with sensors, run an AI model, watch it execute the task. But real-world robotics is considerably more complicated. The problem isn't just in training AI to comprehend, but in training it to respond in a safe and predictable physical manner. The disconnect Between Digital Nerves And Physical Action Think about an industrial robotic arm on an assembly line. The camera detects an item, and the model uses the image to work out where it is. From there, it knows where the robot arm needs to move.

articles.title: Boulder is a CA stack, and its ACME front door is not a title match
articles.excerpt: Boulder is a CA stack, and its ACME front door is not a title match Boulder is the certificate authority software behind Let's Encrypt. It implements ACME, issues certificates, validates domain contro…
articles.body: Boulder is a CA stack, and its ACME front door is not a title match Boulder is the certificate authority software behind Let's Encrypt. It implements ACME, issues certificates, validates domain control, and coordinates several internal services. A Boulder deployment is not a generic web application with one login page. The public ACME front end, the registration authority, the storage layer, and the internal gRPC services have different network and identity requirements. The ZoomEye sample used app="Boulder" and title="Boulder" with page 1, page size 1, and sub_type=all on November 26, 2026. The application query returned 0. The title query returned 3,725. The title value is generic enough to include place names, unrelated software, certificates, and pages about the city of Boulder.

articles.title: Getting a PDF under the LinkedIn document limit: 100 MB and 300 pages
articles.excerpt: A LinkedIn document post takes a PDF, but it has to pass two checks at once: 100 MB or less, and 300 pages or less. LinkedIn's help page words it as "The file size cannot exceed 100MB and 300 pages."…
articles.body: A LinkedIn document post takes a PDF, but it has to pass two checks at once: 100 MB or less, and 300 pages or less. LinkedIn's help page words it as "The file size cannot exceed 100MB and 300 pages." A deck that fails one check will not pass by fixing the other. This is how to find out which one you broke and fix just that. 1. Check both numbers On Linux or macOS, with poppler installed: pdfinfo deck.pdf | grep Pages ls -l deck.pdf With qpdf, which also reports a broken file instead of guessing: qpdf --show-npages deck.pdf qpdf --check deck.pdf Windows and macOS file properties give the size, and any PDF viewer gives the page count. 2. Too many pages: split by range Do not compress a file that is over 300 pages, because compressing keeps every page.

articles.title: Android just had one of its worst quarters, and Apple is benefiting

articles.body: TL;DR Android accounted for 74% of global smartphone sales in Q3 2026, down five points from a year ago and its lowest-ever share for a third quarter, per Counterpoint Research. iOS climbed to a record Q3 share of 21% as iPhone sales grew year-on-year, even as the overall market shrank 16%. HarmonyOS held at 5% globally and took 22% of China’s market, with HUAWEI growing 12% while China’s market shrank 10%. The memory shortage has been dragging down phone sales all year, and new data shows it may be hurting Android more than its rivals. According to Counterpoint Research , global smartphone sales fell 16% year-on-year in Q3 2026, a sharper drop than the 11% decline seen in Q2. Android’s share of those sales slipped to 74%, down from 79% in Q3 2025.

articles.title: Venus shines at its brightest in the predawn sky this week. Here's where to look
articles.excerpt: Venus reaches peak brightness in the predawn sky this week, here's how to find it.
articles.body: Venus is at its most dazzling in the predawn sky this week as it shines close to the bright star Spica in the southeast. Here's what you need to know. As an inner planet, Venus never strays far from the horizon, at least compared to outer planets like Jupiter and Mars which can be visible all night long during opposition, when they shine opposite the sun in Earth's sky. Instead, Venus alternates between morning and evening appearances. All the while, its shifting moon-like phases and ever-changing proximity to Earth causes its brightness to wax and wane. When is Venus at its most dazzling? Venus will reach peak brightness during its current morning apparition at 1:37 p.m. EST (1837 GMT) on Nov. 27 according to the astronomy website In-The-Sky . articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 26, 2011: NASA's 2-ton nuclear-powered Curiosity rover launches to Mars
articles.excerpt: On November 26, 2011, the NASA Curiosity rover launched to Mars. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On November 26, 2011, the NASA Curiosity rover launched to Mars. The Mars rover Curiosity was the biggest and most powerful rover anyone had ever sent to the Red Planet. The 2-ton science laboratory is about the size of a small SUV. The mission's goal was to search for habitable environments on Mars , or evidence that the planet could have been habitable in the past. It launched on an Atlas V rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. About nine months later, Curiosity made a challenging landing on Mars. It successfully used a new landing technology called a sky crane to gently lower it to the surface. NASA's Curiosity rover lifts off atop a United Launch Alliance Atlas V rocket on Nov. 26, 2011 from Florida's Cape Canaveral Air Force Station.
